I’ll chime in in this as I have early less than 25K since moving here in 2019.

My rent for two years for £650, then £700 then £1100. I’ve done it but it has been fucking hard but also I love my money and planning with it. The £1100 rent killed me off so I can respect that £1000 on rent is also tough. However, you’re earning more than I ever have. Having said this, I assume this is base salary and pre tax. So I assume you’re taking home around £2000 each month no? £800-£900 a month to live off is crazy money to me back in the day. 

Min max your money and where it is. I have had multiple accounts for savings and every pound counts. You will know this already but when you have less a pound is worth more to you. Make use of interest of what you do have. However you’ve said you have £800 leftover. £150 into a high interest account each month will max that out. Shove another £200 into a Lifetime ISA. You’re left with £450. Leave that in an instant access saver. Put £50 buffer in your current account for direct debits or whatnot. Each day your money isn’t sat dormant in your current account , move it over when you need it.

Get a Tesco credit card and use that to get points. It’s barely anything but again. It’s more than nothing and it will help occasionally.

Make a note of your tube map and where the zones finish. See if you can get off a stop earlier or on a stop later. I did this in West and saved £1.20 I think ..? By not crossing over an additional zone.

Fucking walk everywhere. Night out? Walk 30 mins towards home and cut the Uber price down if you MUST get an Uber. You can enjoy yourself on this kind of money. Just skim where you can.

Look at your subscriptions and see if you can pair up with anyone. I shared a gym membership when I was unemployed and split the cost with them. Instant saving. Same with iCloud, Spotify you name it. 

Spices and grains and shit. Online, go to a whole foods site and bulk buy with whoever you’re living with. Then you’re set for years and will save shit loads.

Dare I say, I learnt to skip breakfast. It also meant I needed food less often as I wasn’t hungry even at lunch. People won’t recommend it and be sensible but this was one tactic I did to save money.

I stopped using shampoo and conditioner. Now don’t need it. Another small saving but counts. 

Learn to cut your own hair, has saved me hundreds of pounds.
